questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to choose the best new smartphone
Why young people use their phones too much
How to repair an old phone
Why people are keeping their phones for longer
questions.why: They discuss smartphones and why people hold onto their phones instead of buying the latest model.

questions.q: What does Rob say about his own phone?
options: He bought it last month to replace a broken one
It's about two years old and he's happy with it
It often stops working when the battery is low
He plans to upgrade it soon to the newest model
questions.why: Rob bought it a couple of years ago and says it does everything he needs.

questions.q: Why isn't Rob worried about not having the latest model?
options: He doesn't believe the new model offers much more
He can't afford a new phone on his current salary
He doesn't use his phone very often, except for calls
He prefers phones from smaller, cheaper brands
questions.why: He says he's 'not convinced that the latest model offers any more' than his phone.

questions.q: According to Andrew Orlowski, what has happened to expensive phones?
options: Their prices have fallen
Fewer brands make them
Their prices have gone up
They have become smaller
questions.why: He says 'prices have gone up at the high end'.

questions.q: What is the 'cycle' Andrew Orlowski describes?
options: People buy new phones every year, so the prices keep dropping
Makers release new models, so people upgrade more and more often
Phones are kept longer, so prices rise, so people keep them longer
Shops sell old phones cheaply, so makers stop making new ones
questions.why: People hang onto phones longer, makers charge more, then people hang on longer to justify the price.

questions.q: How does Andrew Orlowski describe the smartphone market now?
options: Very new and growing fast
Very mature
About to disappear
Mostly for young people
questions.why: He says 'I think it's a very mature market now'.

questions.q: Why does Andrew Orlowski mention a 49-inch TV for £450?
options: To advertise a TV he likes
To show that TVs are better quality than phones
To suggest people watch TV more than they use phones
To show that expensive phones no longer seem so special
questions.why: He compares £900–£1000 phones with a cheap spectacular TV and says phones lost their 'must-have lustre'.

questions.q: How does Catherine react to the TV example?
options: She thinks the TV sounds like a bargain
She says she never watches TV
She thinks £450 is too expensive
She says her TV is even bigger
questions.why: She says a 49-inch TV for £450 sounds like a bargain, as hers is only 30 inches.
